thread.title: Stock Market Update: Stocks Fall on U.S-China Skepticism, Flattening Yield Curve

title: Stock Market Update: Stocks Fall on U.S-China Skepticism, Flattening Yield Curve
text:
Stocks Fall on U.S-China Skepticism, Flattening Yield Curve 04-Dec-18 13:00 ET Dow -539.39 at 25285.94, Nasdaq -180.90 at 7260.82, S&P -59.03 at 2731.61
[BRIEFING.COM] The S&P 500 has pulled back from yesterday's trade-relief rally with a loss of 2.0% in a broad-based retreat. The broader market has succumbed to some skepticism surrounding U.S.-China trade negotiations; worries that a flattening/inversion of the Treasury yield curve is a sign of slower growth, if not a recession, in the future; and a technical breach of the S&P 500's 200-day moving average (2762.32).
Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is down 2.1%, the Nasdaq Composite is down 2.4%, and the Russell 2000 is down 3.3%.
Investors have expressed concerns over the ability of the U.S. and China being able to reach a deal in just 90 days to settle major trade issues, despite President Donald Trump's optimism. Adding to the skepticism has been the fact that U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer, a China hard-liner, will be leading trade negotiations. The festering doubt has also provided an excuse to take some money off the table following a 6.0% gain for the S&P 500 over the last six trading sessions.
Plenty of attention is being paid to the Treasury market today, which was seemingly relegated to an afterthought during Monday's trade-relief rally that lifted global equity markets. The main talking point has been the inversion seen earlier today between the 2-yr and 3-yr note yields, versus the 5-yr yield, as well as the continued narrowing of the 10-2 spread, which is just 12 basis points now, marking its narrowest spread since 2007.
The moves by the Treasury market have piqued concerns about a future slowdown in growth that have undercut the cyclical sectors.
Within the S&P sectors, the financials (-3.5%), industrials (-3.2%), consumer discretionary (-2.7%), and information technology (-2.7%) sectors have underperformed the broader market.
The financial sector in particular has been pressured by the flattening/inversion action in the U.S. Treasury market, which is raising concerns about earnings prospects.
Regional banks have been notable laggards as worries about lower mortgage loan demand have germinated on the back of the acknowledgment from home builder Toll Brothers (TOL 33.07, -0.46, -1.4%) that it saw a moderation in demand in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Oct. 31 and that it saw the market soften further in November. The SPDR S&P Regional Bank ETF (KRE 52.91, -2.77) is down 5.0%.
Within the tech space, another Apple (AAPL 178.42, -6.47, -3.5%) supplier warning has weighed on the sector and chip stocks. Chip supplier Cirrus Logic (CRUS 38.13, -0.55, -1.4%) lowered its revenue guidance due to recent weaknesses in the smartphone market. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index struggles with a loss of 3.4%.
Also underperforming today have been transport stocks with the Dow Jones Transportation Average tumbling 4.1%. Notable laggards include UPS (UPS 107.07, -8.16) and American Airlines (AAL 37.31, -2.36) with respective losses of 7.1% and 6.0%.
Conversely, the lightly-weighted utilities sector (+0.8%) is the only group sporting gains today. The defensive-oriented real estate (-0.4%) and consumer staples (-0.5%) sectors also show relative strength.
Investors did not receive any notable economic data today.
